subject.title: fix(openshell): bound sandbox readFile with size cap

question: Should OpenShell adopt an unconditional 100 MiB maximum for every sandbox `readFile` request as its shipped compatibility and memory-safety contract?
rationale: The cap fixes the reported host-memory exposure but deliberately changes behavior for previously readable large sandbox files; the repository policy treats security/fallback and compatibility boundaries as maintainer decisions.

options.title: Adopt the 100 MiB boundary
options.body: Accept the fixed cap, then require direct normal-read and over-limit runtime proof before merging.

options.title: Choose another supported policy
options.body: Specify a different cap or an owner-approved compatibility design before changing the sandbox read contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt the 100 MiB boundary
recommendation.body: Accept the fixed cap, then require direct normal-read and over-limit runtime proof before merging.

likelyOwner.reason: No current-main OpenShell ownership history was available in the supplied read-only context, so naming a specific person would be speculation.
